description.short_caption: Axial head CT scan showing multiple hypodense lesions.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT scan of the head reveals multiple hypodense lesions scattered throughout the brain parenchyma. The lesions vary in size and are suggestive of space-occupying processes. There is no clear evidence of midline shift or significant mass effect. The scan is non-contrast, as no enhancement is visible.
visible_findings: multiple hypodense lesions in the brain parenchyma

description.short_caption: GMS stain showing fungal hyphae and spores.
description.detailed_description: This is a microscopic image stained with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS), highlighting fungal elements. The fungal hyphae appear as black, branching structures against a greenish-blue background. Rounded fungal spores are also visible. The stain is commonly used to identify fungal organisms in tissue samples.
visible_findings: greenish-blue background typical of GMS stain

description.short_caption: Special stain showing filamentous branching organisms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic field stained with a special stain, likely a modified acid-fast or Gram stain. Filamentous, branching organisms are visible, appearing as darkly stained structures against a lighter background. The surrounding field contains amorphous material and cellular debris, suggesting an infectious or inflammatory process. The morphology is consistent with filamentous bacteria, such as Nocardia or Actinomyces.

This image shows a Fite stain, a specialized staining technique used to identify acid-fast organisms. Numerous blue-stained background cells are visible, likely representing host tissue or inflammatory cells. Thin, elongated, pink-stained structures consistent with acid-fast bacilli are seen, indicative of organisms such as Mycobacterium species. The bacilli are scattered and appear as slender, curved rods.
